steps.name: Gaunt Monastery Inhabitant
steps.text: There you are, Father.

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: It's your turn to clean the chapel today, Jori?

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: Gratias.

steps.name: Jori
steps.text: Just doing my job. I had trouble sleeping anyway.

steps.name: Jori
steps.text: I'll fetch the sacramental bread.

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: No, no need.

steps.name: Jori
steps.text: Oh, right, look at me, dust all over my hands.

steps.name: Jori
steps.text: Say, do you smell something...? It's pretty faint...

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: A strange smell?

steps.name: Jori
steps.text: No, a pleasant one. It's fresh. I sense in it... vitality.

steps.name: Jori
steps.text: It's hard to put into words. It's like standard downwind. I don't know where it comes from, but I feel like I'd get somewhere if I followed it.

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: I think it's the smell of flowers, Jori.

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: We don't have enough flour, so flower powder was added to the sacramental bread.

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: The few remaining bottles of wine in the cellar have started to go sour, so I also added some flower powder to those too.

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: Clément harvested some flowers a couple of years ago, grinding them into powder and storing it in the cellar...

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: He loves the flowers, just as he loves us.

steps.name: Jori
steps.text: Mm...

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: This will be the final communion we take before the abbey departs. We are short on food, however, so we must reduce each share of sacramental bread, even mixing in... other grains.

steps.name: Jori
steps.text: Please don't say that. I'm very much looking forward to today's communion...

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: Then go and wash your face. Come back with the others when it's time for Matins.

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: I'll do the rest myself.

steps.name: Jori
steps.text: Yes, Father.

steps.name: Jori
steps.text: Will we be saved after today, Father?

steps.name: Jori
steps.text: All of us, Sankta and Sarkaz... will we all be saved?

steps.name: Jori
steps.text: Even though Gerald is already...

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: Go, Jori.

steps.name: Jori
steps.text: O-Okay, see you later, Father.
The old man closes the door.
He climbs the chancel slowly.
Stefano Torregrossa, the aging abbot of Sanctilaminium Ambrosii, carefully divides the sacramental bread and wine.
His head is bowed. It is still early. The dim morning light shines through the windows behind the holy statue. The face of the statue is hidden in darkness, as is the abbot's own.

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: Yes. We will all be saved.
She walks into the broken sacrarium, crushing the charred remains of plants to powder beneath her feet.
The arched roof of the sacrarium has collapsed in the fire, exposing the interior in the sunlight.
The wind has carried away the smell, but there is no one to clean up the rubble.
The marks of the fire will remain forever, unless the chapel is rebuilt.
She takes a look at the collapsed statue, then abruptly turns to the empty space behind her.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Humans struggle, punish and forgive themselves, like a sonata at its climax, the keys dancing a frantic tune.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: When a decision is made, the long and steady coda begins, the emptiness at the end of catharsis, yet infinitely determined.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Emotions are complex, but the changes are always alike. The melody is conventional, regular, devoid of surprise.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: I sense your serenity. You have made your choice.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: In any case, the song I should play is you. Hear the voice of your own heart, here at the very end.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: You lost, vibrant soul.

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: All the pots and chopping boards... signs of baking, but no smell of yeast in the air... oh, I guess it's unleavened bread.

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: This looks like they were preparing the Eucharist here.

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: There is unidentified debris... it feels wet. Is it because we're underground?

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: No.

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: There is flour left in the corner... why is it so damp and sticky?

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: This smell...

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: Is this the only path the pious abbot saw, at the end of it all?

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: Can't get in touch with Federico... tell Oren? That will only make things more complicated.

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: Am I the one who's going to have to do this? I barely know where Iberia even is.

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: This is such a headache.

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: My forces will soon surround the monastery...

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: I will command them to block every path in and out. You stay here and coordinate with the assault.

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: Mm...

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: What is it?

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: Are you sure you want to do this, Oren?

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: Did you go over to Lemuen's side the moment you saw her? I don't think I need to waste my time explaining this again.
But I'll stop you, Oren.

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: Lemuen?

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: Ugh. She caught up.

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: Buy time while I rendezvous with the troops.

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: No way. Do you see the expression on her face?

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: I'm not getting on her bad side. I still remember when she dragged me out of school and confiscated my drone. I never saw it again.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: Gratias, Serpilia.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: You never thought to convince the abbot to bring the monastery back to Laterano.

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: That's your job.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: You never intended to let any of the Sarkaz leave, you've even got commandos deployed to carry out your plan.

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: Fifty men... the limit of what I can muster.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: What are the Lateran laws to you, Oren?

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: I will submit myself to His Holiness's judgment when we get back... though I don't think I've done anything that should be punished.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: You know the consequences of an assault on the abbey.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: The people here, both Sankta and Sarkaz, are like travelers who lost their way in the wilderness, who found warmth by a campfire.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: The campfire guides their kin to rescue them, and other poor wandering souls.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: They have no one to count on. They are weak and frightened. But they still hold on to their precious kindness.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: That's why Gerald gave his life to plead with us, and ordered the Sarkaz under his leadership to keep the peace between the two sides.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: But what if the campfire has attracted some beasts?

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: I wish I could say pretty words and do the kind of work everyone admires, Cardinal Aide Lemuen.

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: But I can't. You've never traveled the war-torn wastes with thousands upon thousands of refugees, seen the dark cloud that blankets the skies over Londinium.

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: But I thought you would at least have a tacit understanding with me, give some thought to the danger in letting those Sarkaz go.

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: The atrocities the Sarkaz committed in Victoria are well-known. They continue to spread their terror across the lands.

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: If you truly believe in His Holiness's plan, believe in the value of the Legati, then you should understand why Laterano can't be merciful here.

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: The friendship that Laterano built at the Summit of Nations is more fragile than the paper windows of this corridor.

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: The Sarkaz in the abbey are resentful, and affected by Arturia's Arts. There's no telling what lengths they will go to in order to get revenge after they leave.

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: Plus, what would happen if word got out that a Lateran nomadic abbey has been colluding with the Sarkaz for decades?

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: How will Laterano uphold its sanctity among the nations of Terra? How will she maintain her already-fragile diplomatic ties?

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: What will the Holy City look like when the fires of war burn?

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: Fifty men. That's all will take to resolve the situation here, and bury it all in darkness.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: These Sarkaz are hunters, farmers... the only mercenary is dead. We saw proof with our own eyes.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: You're planning a massacre.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: You talk about upholding Laterano's sanctity, when you're the one defiling it. Don't you see the hypocrisy in that?

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: You're the hypocrite here, Lemuen.

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: The 'Lemuen the Silent' I know wouldn't have blinked at something like this.

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: Did five years asleep change you?

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: Or was it the so-called 'Martyr'—
Oren never managed to say the name.

The wheelchair closes the distance in the blink of an eye, and his midsection meets the barrel of a sniper rifle. Leaning against the wall, he barely manages to stay on his feet, and it takes all his effort to keep his voice level.

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: Gah—

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: Go on.

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: ...Lemuen the Silent.

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: I told you not to get on her bad side.

steps.name: Young Lateran Commando
steps.text: Team Two at target location. Charges set.

steps.name: Young Lateran Commando
steps.text: All three exits on the blueprints of Sanctilaminium Ambrosii are under control.

steps.name: Young Lateran Commando
steps.text: If anyone tries to get out, the explosion will collapse the passage and force them back...

steps.name: Veteran Lateran Commando
steps.text: More like bury them under the rubble. Team Two was laughing about not being too precise here.

steps.name: Veteran Lateran Commando
steps.text: Go ahead.

steps.name: Young Lateran Commando
steps.text: Teams Three and Four have taken the high ground. We have sniper cover in all directions.

steps.name: Young Lateran Commando
steps.text: All teams in position.

steps.name: Veteran Lateran Commando
steps.text: Right on time.

steps.name: Veteran Lateran Commando
steps.text: Reverend Oren, we are in position to begin the assault on the Sarkaz in the abbey.

steps.name: Veteran Lateran Commando
steps.text: Repeat: We are in position.

steps.name: Young Lateran Commando
steps.text: What is it?

steps.name: Veteran Lateran Commando
steps.text: No response.

steps.name: Young Lateran Commando
steps.text: ...That's not good.

steps.name: Veteran Lateran Commando
steps.text: Ha, don't worry about it. He probably has his hands full with an extra-large crepe.

steps.name: Young Lateran Commando
steps.text: Does that happen a lot?

steps.name: Veteran Lateran Commando
steps.text: All the time. First time on a special operation? Chill. The Lateran watches over you.

steps.name: Veteran Lateran Commando
steps.text: Just make sure you're ready. We'll go in the front door if we can't reach Oren, or if there's any unusual activity.

steps.name: Raimund
steps.text: No one in the hallway. Quick, this way.

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: That way leads out the abbey. Aren't we looking for Gerald?

steps.name: Raimund
steps.text: No, I need to get you to safety first.

steps.name: Raimund
steps.text: Didn't you hear? The Laterans are taking the abbey by force. That woman, Serpilia, might have played nice, but the army won't.

steps.name: Raimund
steps.text: You can't be seen by the Lateran army. You're fallen. To them, you're evi...

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: Go ahead, Raimund. I can handle it.

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: Don't... don't let me interrupt you, I did Fina.

steps.name: Raimund
steps.text: All I meant to say is that you've never changed, not to me, Fortuna.

steps.name: Raimund
steps.text: Anyway, you're in the same boat we are. It's only going to mean more trouble for the others if you stay behind.

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: ...Alright.

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: I'll do as you say.

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: But what about you, Raimund? Will you be alright?

steps.name: Raimund
steps.text: Don't worry, Gerald made plans for everything. I'm sure he anticipated something like this.

steps.name: Raimund
steps.text: I'll come back and help him once I've found a safe place for you.

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: Your palms are sweating, Raimund. What's going on?

steps.name: Raimund
steps.text: Nothing, just... a feeling I can't describe, like a heavy weight...

steps.name: Raimund
steps.text: Maybe it's just that I didn't eat breakfast.

steps.name: Raimund
steps.text: If not for all this, we would be having communion right now, with Gerald and everyone else...

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: We'll have plenty of chances.

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: Take a deep breath, Raimund. I'll be the one pulling you along now.

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: This way. The rooms here are all empty. No one will see us.

steps.name: Raimund
steps.text: I'm fine. We're almost to the front door.

steps.name: Raimund
steps.text: The Laterans might hear us opening the door. We go right as soon as we're outside. The rocks and tall grass should provide cover.

steps.name: Raimund
steps.text: Are you ready? I pulled the latch.

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: Th-This is...

steps.name: Raimund
steps.text: So that's why I had a feeling. Lateran troops.

steps.name: Raimund
steps.text: Stay behind me, Fortuna.

steps.name: Veteran Lateran Commando
steps.text: ...Team One here. Sarkaz sighted at the front door.
